source: IRS Revenue Procedure 2025-32; SSA Contribution and Benefit Base Announcement (2026)
notes: 2026 brackets and standard deductions reflect the OBBBA-adjusted, inflation-indexed figures per IRS Rev. Proc. 2025-32.

Federal withholding in payroll engines normally uses IRS Publication 15-T percentage method tables (which annualize wages differently from the year-end tax brackets shown here). This engine approximates annualized effective withholding by applying marginal brackets to annualized taxable wages, then dividing by pay periods — sufficient for an estimator tool, not for exact employer withholding compliance.

Additional Medicare Tax (0.9%) is withheld by employers once an individual employee's wages exceed $200,000 in a calendar year, regardless of filing status — the threshold column above reflects the year-end return threshold, but calculator.ts applies the $200,000 single-employer withholding rule as is standard payroll practice.
Social Security wage base for 2026 is $184,500 (up from $176,100 in 2025), yielding a max employee contribution of $11,439.00.
